## The termination logic, in full

`dispatch_stop_reason()` is the heart of TS 1.1 and the one piece of this repo
worth reading closely. It is **pure** — it reads `stop_reason` and nothing else,
takes no client, performs no I/O, and never inspects response *text*. That is
what makes the loop's termination auditable and unit-testable.

The listing below is sliced live out of
[`01-agentic-loops/orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/project-delphi/claude-architect-prep/blob/main/01-agentic-loops/orchestrator.py)
at render time, so it cannot drift from the code that actually runs.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pathlib import Path

src = Path("../01-agentic-loops/orchestrator.py").read_text().splitlines()
start = src.index("# docs:start dispatch_stop_reason") + 1
end = src.index("# docs:end dispatch_stop_reason")
print("```python")
print("\n".join(src[start:end]))
print("```")
```

**An unrecognised `stop_reason` raises rather than returns.** Failing loudly
beats silently treating an unknown state as completion — the exact anti-pattern
TS 1.1 asks about.
